extracted.intended_audience: NLP/CL researchers and practitioners, tutorial organizers, and ethics reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for designing and running a participatory ethics tutorial in NLP (activities, slide/segment content, facilitation structure) and for leading group abstract-critique exercises on ethical issues in NLP research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit number of groups for timely presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: limit the number of groups so that each group could present within the session's time limit;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the number of groups is small enough for all groups to present within the allotted session time. This interacts with facilitator-to-group ratio — fewer groups or more facilitators are required to let all participants reflect, contribute, and be heard while keeping the session on track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate organiser to facilitate virtual participants
rubrics_metrics.description: designate a particular organiser to facilitate virtual participants;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign a specific organiser responsible for supporting and integrating remote attendees during the session (e.g., monitoring chat, ensuring virtual groups have parity, relaying virtual questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide live-edit access to shared documents
rubrics_metrics.description: have live edit access to online documents, to allow participant leads to note take and present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collaborative documents/slides with live-edit permissions for group scribes and presenters so they can take notes, prepare slides, and present directly during the session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator-to-group ratio requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This required a good facilitator-to-group ratio, to ensure all of the participants had a chance to reflect, contribute and be heard, and for the facilitators to keep the session on track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan sufficient facilitators relative to groups so facilitators can probe groups, maintain focus, and ensure equitable participation. Adjust number of groups or facilitator assignments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create local shortlinks/URL codes before running
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimally, you need to create your own shortlinks and URL codes to your version of the materials before running, as the archived materials reference our EACL 2023 instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare working links to slides, docs, and activity artifacts in advance; scrubbed/archived materials reference the original instance and must be relinked for your event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecture-only format: use segments 1 and 7 material
rubrics_metrics.description: Lecture only: use and adapt the lecture materials from the first and seventh segments of the tutorial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If running a purely lecture-based session, adapt the slides/content from Segment 1 (foundations/definitions) and Segment 7 (ethical consideration sections) to cover foundational and paper-focused ethics topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiential-only format: use segments 2-6 for abstract critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiential only: use and adapt Segments 2-6, which asks participants to read and critique abstracts that bring up common ethical issues in our community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a hands-on workshop, use the case-study segments (2–6) and the provided problematic abstracts to run group critique exercises focusing on recurring ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student/Homework assignment: use Ethics Reading List
rubrics_metrics.description: Student (Homework) Assignment: curate sources from the accompanying Ethics Reading List that the committee maintains, and ask participants to read and write their reflections on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign readings from the maintained Ethics Reading List and require written reflections to extend learning outside the workshop session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use small-group structure with elected scribe and presenter
rubrics_metrics.description: participants were self-organized into small groups (in our instance, 2 groups of about 10 participants each), electing leads for subsequent group presentation and worked through the exercises to record their reactions to the materials and identify the issues and conducive outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize participants into small groups and have each group elect a scribe (note-taker) and a presenter (speaker). This supports shared responsibility and structured reporting back to the full audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity roles: scribe and presenter responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The scribe serves as a secretariat for typing in the notes from their group; and the presenter is delegated as the person in the group to present the findings to the entire tutorial audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify role responsibilities in advance: scribes should record group discussion in the shared document/slides; presenters should summarize and present group conclusions clearly during plenary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase abstract critique process
rubrics_metrics.description: The critique of the abstracts is run in two phases. In the first phase, groups discuss first to prepare a single slide for silent sharing with other groups (Segment 2). In this second phase (Segment 4), the groups could enlarge their thinking by reflecting on either additional abstracts, the single shared slide from each group, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1: quick group discussion producing one slide for silent sharing. Phase 2: reflection/rotation where groups review other groups' slides and/or additional abstracts and expand their analysis. Use facilitators to probe for depth and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slide limits for group work
rubrics_metrics.description: we used an editable online presentation deck such that each group could create 1-3 slides (1 slide max in the first phease)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce slide limits to keep group outputs concise: max 1 slide in phase 1, up to 3 slides total in later phases. Use shared decks so groups can rapidly create and present slides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group presentation & facilitator probing
rubrics_metrics.description: After both phases were finished, each group presented elements of their findings, with the faciltators structuring and probing for issues and clarity on different aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During presentations, facilitators should structure Q&A, ask probing questions to surface ethical issues, and clarify points about harms, benefits, and affected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment 1A content: foundations of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment 1A (Slides 6-39) covers the definition and scope of ethics; its origins; virtue, deontological and utilitarian forms of ethics; experiments and policy reactions to ethical violation (Nuremburg Trials and Code, Belmont Report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include foundational ethical theory (virtue, deontology, utilitarianism) and historical regulatory/ethical reaction cases to ground discussion about research ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment 1B content: appropriate use, biases, and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment 1B (Slides 40-70) focuses on appropriate use and application, biases and evaluation, covering hypothetical and real instances of ethical problems in recent research (Chicken dilemma, IQ prediction, sexual orientation prediction -- the "Gaydar" paper, and how AI and NLP technology influences people both directly and indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover concrete examples of ethical issues in NLP (problematic tasks, biased applications), methods for assessing bias, and considerations of appropriate use and downstream impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment 7A content: evaluating Ethical Consideration Sections (ECS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment 7A (Slides 86-99) reprised work from Benotti and Blackburn (2022) Ethical Consideration Sections in Natural Language Processing Papers, which examined such written ECS in NLP papers to analyze the issues covered in terms of 1) research benefits, 2) potential harms, and 3) vulnerable groups affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating ECS in papers, analyze whether authors discuss research benefits, potential harms, and identify vulnerable groups affected; be mindful of geographic differences in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scrubbed/archived materials responsibly and request access if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: (Due to the sensitive nature of our EACL 2023 participants' contribution, we have scrubbed the QR coded and shortlinked materials of their presence; if any party wants to access the original document we have these archived but not in this repository nor linked to here; please contact us directly)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original un-scrubbed materials are needed, contact the organisers to request archived versions; be aware that shared materials in the repository may have personally identifying details removed.
